Verify that the intended connection is between compatible 2.5-inch hose cuffs, not merely a nominal 2.5-inch dust port, and test the fit before relying on it. Prefer an exact-fit coupling if available; do not plan to cut hose fittings or treat tape as a substitute for a secure connection in demanding use.

Comes with a full complement of jumpers.

Just recieved my second board from HiLetGo. The original is still working really well. The new board seems to be working just fine on an Arduino Mega Clone. My only complaint is the solder points under the main power input on both boards needed to be filed down a significant amount to allow for installation on the Arduino Mega.

6/7/2019

Suitable use cases include low to moderate current 3D printer setups where budget constraints are significant and users have electronics experience to inspect and possibly repair the board before use. It can be used for troubleshooting or as a temporary replacement in traditional RepRap style 3D printers. Unsuitable use cases include high current applications (e.g., above 30 amps), large or complex installations, or any scenario where safety and reliability are critical due to multiple reports of MOSFET failures and fire hazards. It is also not recommended for users without technical skills to verify board integrity and perform necessary modifications.

Evidence calibration: 4 of 12 supplied reviews (33.3%) report a clear failure or user intervention, exceeding the 20% threshold. Product data: {"name": "JYETech 'DSO Shell' Oscilloscope DIY Kit w/Enclosure, 100MHz Probe, Clip Probe & ESD-Safe Silicone Mat", "brand_or_store": "NooElec", "category": "Computers", "subcategories": ["Industrial & Scientific", "Test, Measure & Inspect", "Electrical Testing", "Oscilloscopes & Accessories", "Oscilloscopes"], "features": ["Build your own color oscilloscope! Basic through-hole soldering skills are required (surface mount parts are pre-soldered to PCB)", "Purchase includes full oscilloscope kit with parts, plastic enclosure, 100MHz oscilloscope probe, additional alligator clip probe, and ESD-safe mat for protecting your desk while soldering", "Printed instructions, troubleshooting guide and schematic are also included", "Contains a 2.4\" color TFT LCD (320x240) display and optical encoder for navigation", "DSO150 (15001K) kit is an upgrade to the popular DSO138 scope kit"], "technical_details": {"Brand": "NooElec", "Item model number": "DSO Shell Bundle", "Item Weight": "10.6 ounces", "Package Dimensions": "12.76 x 9.92 x 3.19 inches", "Manufacturer": "NooElec Inc.", "Is Discontinued By Manufacturer": "No", "Date First Available": "April 4, 2017", "Best Sellers Rank": {"Industrial & Scientific": 333319, "Lab Oscilloscopes": 220, "Lab Meters": 4300}, "Platform": "Not Machine Specific", "Surround Sound Channel Configuration": "5 1", "Maximum Sample Rate": "1 Mega Samples per Second"}, "price_usd": 49.95, "catalog_average_rating": 3.9, "catalog_rating_count": 125} Selected evidence: [{"id": "R1", "rating": 2.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 25, "title": "Missing part, outdated hardware and firmware", "text": "I got the package that contained DSO Shell kit, a nicely looking x1/x10 test probe and a somewhat smallish silicone pad.

The kit missed the square wave signal contact.
The PCB board is version x.00D while the current version is x.00E with much better power supply handling.
The preinstalled firmware is very old: v.x53. Since then at least three releases have happened: x55, x60, x61.
Note that the firmware upgrade process is not a trivial one and needs a special UART-to-USB circuit board and some additional soldering.
For me, the firmware issue is not a negative but it might be a problem for others.

After considering the missing contact tab and old PCB version I returned the package.

I guess I need to wait until sellers upgrade their surplus to the latest PCB version.
After that, I'll gladly update the review."}, {"id": "R2", "rating": 1.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 1, "title": "Kit has error, not able to get help fixing", "text": "I received this kit, and was able to assemble it in a day. I'm an experienced electronics technician and have assembled a lot of electronics kits and built a lot of circuits from scratch before. The assemble went smoothly. A big aid is that all Surface Mounted Technology (SMT) parts were already assembled on the two boards.
I was able to power up the oscilloscope as I was assembling it, and everything worked fine. However, if I screwed down the front 'frame' (around the front panel), I get an '0x9341' error on the second start-up screen and the unit freezes. When the front frame is removed, it works correctly. Because it works correctly when unfastened, I don't think I made any errors in assembling the kit.
I tried to post this error to the Manufacturer's (JYETech) forum a week ago, with no responses. I wrote directly to JYETech 5 days ago, with no response. I contacted the sel"}, {"id": "R3", "rating": 1.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 1, "title": "Very poor quality, broken and missing parts", "text": "I am extremely disappointed with this product. The instructions are poorly written, and they are clearly made for a different hardware/firmware version than what is shipped. The screen shots look different that what my device displays, and the calibration instructions do not match up with the options displayed on screen.

To top it off, my device was shipped with a broken C5 adjustment capacitor. The disk between the base and the adjustment screw was broken into 3 pieces. This makes calibration of the device impossible. The included 1/10X probe was also missing a piece (the ground spring).

I really wanted to like this product, its a very cool idea. Unfortunately the quality and documentation are quite poor. Save your money and time and look for something better."}, {"id": "R4", "rating": 1.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 1, "title": "Broken LCD module... Quality control problem?", "text": "When I opened the box and powered the main module first time as instructed in the Assembly Step, I found that the LCD module is badly cracked. The screen crack is too severe to display anything... So I never got to complete the assembly and to try out the device performance or accuracy."}, {"id": "R5", "rating": 3.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 0, "title": "Gets the job done, just doesn't have a battery", "text": "For $40, I can't complain much. It was easy to assemble, following the directions. Works as described. I really like the rotary encoder compared to the \"push button only\" interface of similar devices. The only draw back is the lack of a battery. I ended up mounting a panel mount 9V connector to the bottom of the case so when I use it, there is a 9V battery sticking out of the bottom. It was $40, though, so who really cares."}, {"id": "R6", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 16, "title": "Jr Maker tool. Sr. helper tool.", "text": "accidently ordered 2, and glad i did, these have already proved to be a value to identify problems with a PSU i was using as a bench supply. i did no expect this level of detail from a DIY project at its cost.
the units i recieved have all the markers of official (not fake) units. as this seller is listed as one of their distributors.
the picture shows what should be a clean 12V rail from a old computer PSU, it turns out 2 of my 4 onld PSU's have very bad 12V rails. ive already used it as anyone would to check input signals or pulse power spikes. this is a valuable item for ANY junior electronics enthusiast. (im not junior, but finally pulling gear together and this is my first personal oscilloscope). if you have a young friend, or child interested in electronics. get this for them and get them really excited to see more of their electronics world. its a DIY project, you will b"}, {"id": "R7", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 5, "title": "Hard to Beat this Scope with a Stick, for $40 USD", "text": "I purchased the DIY version of this kit on Amazon from NooElec Inc.on 16 Apr 2018. It arrived plenty quickly. I purchased the version of this JYETech DSO Shell O-Scope kit that did already have the SMD components soldered on, but that needed the regular components: resistors, caps, pots, headers -soldered on. I completed soldering the components in to the board last night, then Itested voltages as per the included JYETech docs and & web page. I also performed their manuf. recommended, internally-supplied test signal calibrations, using the two trim caps. I hadn't soldered any electronic components in quite a while, so I had to go purchase lead free, rosin-core solder from my local H/W store, yesterday evening. I did pre-meter-out all of the solder-able components that I had the capability to measure, before I inserted these in the circuit board and soldered them into place the circuit bo"}, {"id": "R8", "rating": 4.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 2, "title": "I had to build two until the best pieces of each gave me a working meter", "text": "the high meg ohm resisters don,t read on my digital multi meter.It would be wise to surface mount those at the factory, while your at it why not offer a version where all the resisters are surface mounted for an extra charge. I had to build two until the best pieces of each gave me a working meter. The high frequency probe is a big plus.I usually pay to much for them. So getting one with this low cost meter made up for a lot of grief.."}, {"id": "R9", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 1, "title": "Works quite well - at a good price. But I revised the DC power for convenience.", "text": "This handy little low cost scope works well. The encoder based adjustments are quick and intuitive. Instructions are adequate for assembly and startup, no problems encountered. But the 9 volt DC power requirement is a bit oddball. So I bought a little boost converter board MT3608 for one dollar to add inside. I soldered in pi-LC-filters for 5V in and 9 V out , wrapped it all in tape and copper foil ground, and glued a micro USB 5V connector on the main board. Now I can run the scope from a little 5V USB port Li Ion powerpak for portable use , perfectly ground isolated - and it gave NO added signal noise. Hope JYETech will one day go for std USB / 5V input... and why not also expand it for easier data transfer to PC ! And final comment - This small device has a big advantage ove my PC USB scopes: It works very quickly after power up and shows data on the spot, just like your little digita"}, {"id": "R10", "rating": 4.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 1, "title": "A little bit of a pain but worthwhile in the end.", "text": "Well...at first I hated this thing because it only worked for about 45 minutes after I built it. However the website had great information though it took a little hunting. My 7660 IC was getting hot. I swapped out electrolytic capacitors and no go....finally decided it was the IC. Found a slightly larger SMD chip on a broken OBD2 scanner I had and removed it. It fit the lugs just fine and solved the problem.

Here lately I'm getting a little glitch on the screen where the graphics corrupt. Easy enough to reset but hopefully when I update the firmware that will go away. While it looks like a toy it's actually useful for tracing audio signals through a circuit. If I did nothing else it was worth the build (assembly) process and it's cute to look at. I'm happy with it."}] Task: Summarize evidence-supported advantages and limitations.

Pros: The Aokin 5pcs A4988 StepStick driver modules are low cost, making them an economical choice for projects requiring multiple stepper drivers. They support multiple microstepping modes (full to sixteenth-step) and have an output drive capacity up to 35 V and 2 A. The modules fit well with RAMPS boards and control NEMA motors effectively. Cons: The product suffers from quality control issues such as bent pins, poor manufacturing tolerances, and some units arriving used or defective. Documentation is lacking, and the included jumper count is insufficient for full population of all steppers. The orientation picture in the description is incorrect, leading to user errors and damaged drivers. The product requires manual driver installation on Windows due to clone Arduino boards. Some users reported short circuits causing damage to other electronics and potential fire hazards. Overall, the product is not beginner-friendly and requires significant setup knowledge.

Evidence calibration: 5 of 12 supplied reviews (41.7%) report a clear failure or user intervention, exceeding the 20% threshold. Present these reports as buyer checks and as a reason to prefer a more reliable alternative when available. User adjustments and workarounds are observations, not validated operating or safety instructions.

review_reasons: There are contradictory safety reports including a fire hazard and short circuits, and quality issues that may confuse users about reliability and safe use.

***Hint, hit surface of PEI with a very quick spray of cooking oil before printing with PETG. Use a paper towel to spread evenly and lightly. PETG sticks like crazy at 80 C but release really well at 50 C.

Once it was where I wanted it I lowered the right side down to the glass and pressed it down. I was then able to slightly lift the left side and peel away the rest of the backing while using a roller to ensure good contact (I used one that I had around to apply sound deadening material). It came out looking just like the print bed did when new."}, {"id": "R12", "rating": 5.0, "verified_purchase": true, "helpful_votes": 0, "title": "Fixes a bunch of first layer problems", "text": "I was having problems with my A20 printer. I got a glass bed plate to make the bed flatter, but I could not get the first layer to stick reliably even with glue, painters tape, etc...
This sheet fixes all that. Very easy to stick to the glass bed, just make sure everything is very clean. You don't want any speck stuck between the sheet and the bed.

I had to trim the sheet a bit to fit the bed. the material is very tough and it takes a few passed with a knife to get the material thin enough to bend and break. My metal scraper has not gouged the plate yet, but the surface seems a bit 'soft' and I would be careful."}] Task: Summarize evidence-supported advantages and limitations.

Pros: The Gizmo Dorks PEI sheet offers a no-prep, reusable build surface compatible with ABS, PLA, PETG, and other filaments without additional adhesives. It features a laminated 3M 468MP adhesive for quick, bubble-free application and is made in the USA with durable Ultem 1000 PEI. Users report excellent adhesion and easy print release after cooling, with some praising its thickness and durability. Cons: Some users received sheets without adhesive or protective covering, indicating possible quality control or shipping issues. There are reports of uneven glue application and damage during shipping causing ripples or craters in the adhesive. A few users experienced surface damage such as holes or melting on first use, suggesting sensitivity to printing conditions. Once applied, the sheet is difficult to remove, and improper installation can cause adhesion problems.

Evidence calibration: 4 of 12 supplied reviews (33.3%) report a clear failure or user intervention, exceeding the 20% threshold. Present these reports as buyer checks and as a reason to prefer a more reliable alternative when available. User adjustments and workarounds are observations, not validated operating or safety instructions.

review_reasons: Conflicting reports on adhesive presence and surface durability, plus safety concerns about melting and burning, require expert validation.

This caster kit is recommended only if you own a compatible Gladiator modular GearBox cabinet with pre-drilled mounting holes matching the kit's fixed caster orientation. Verify your cabinet model against Gladiator's compatibility list and inspect for mounting hole availability before purchase. Be aware that the fixed front casters and swivel rear casters limit maneuverability, which may impact use in tight spaces. Confirm that the supplied screws are adequate for your cabinet or be prepared to source longer screws. If your cabinet is large or lacks mounting holes, or if you require full swivel casters, consider alternative caster options.
